summary: All five tests prescribed by the TDD Anchor exist and assert what the anchor demands; Test_setFilter was updated in place with named subcases and an explicit order-dependence comment. Every test exercises real production code with concrete assertions — no mock-only tests, no empty tests, litmus test passes on all 17 cases. I independently mutation-tested both regression guards: reverting the in-place delete to a map reassignment makes Test_clearFilters_inPlaceVisibleThroughStoredView fail (not hang), and dropping the `if n > 0` send condition makes Test_clearFilters_noActiveFilters fail in 1.00s with the intended message instead of hanging until the go test timeout — the deadline-guarded goroutine works exactly as the anchor required. Three minor findings remain: the no-filters case never asserts the handler's returned error, the two drain-goroutine tests can still hang instead of failing if the send is lost, and Test_setFilter's subcases are documented as order-dependent but are not independently runnable (`-run Test_setFilter/clear-existing` fails). None of these block the task.

findings.issue: The TDD Anchor demands that on a view without filters 'обработчик возвращает nil', but the test discards the return value: `go func() { defer close(done); _ = clearFilters(config)(nil, nil) }()`. The three sibling tests all assert.NoError on the handler; this path does not. The filters map is also only asserted empty BEFORE the handler runs (line 414) — never after, so a handler that both returned an error and mutated the map on the empty path would go unnoticed. (The anchor's own snippet used `_ =`, so this is a gap in the anchor as much as in the test.)
findings.recommendation:
Capture the error in a variable owned by the test goroutine and assert it after the `<-done` case — closing `done` establishes the happens-before edge, so this is race-free:

```go
var err error
done := make(chan struct{})
go func() { defer close(done); err = clearFilters(config)(nil, nil) }()

select {
case <-done:
	assert.NoError(t, err)
case <-time.After(time.Second):
	t.Fatal("handler blocked sending on viewCh with no filters to clear")
}
assert.Empty(t, config.view.Filters) // map untouched by the handler too
```
Do not read `err` in the timeout branch — only the `<-done` branch is synchronized.

findings.issue: Both tests arm an unguarded drain goroutine (`v := <-config.viewCh; close(config.viewCh); wg.Done()`) and then block on `wg.Wait()`. If a future regression stops the handler from sending — the exact failure mode this task is about, e.g. someone tightening the `if n > 0` condition or adding an early return — the drain goroutine never receives and `wg.Wait()` hangs until the `go test` timeout, taking down the whole `./top` package instead of failing this one case. This is the same hang-vs-fail hazard the anchor went out of its way to eliminate in the sibling Test_clearFilters_noActiveFilters, left unaddressed on the mirror path. It follows the pre-existing file pattern (Test_scrollOrthogonalToSort), which is why this is minor and not major — but those neighbours do not test a conditional send, and these two do.
findings.recommendation:
Replace `wg`/`wg.Wait()` with a deadline in both tests, mirroring the guard already used in Test_clearFilters_noActiveFilters:

```go
received := make(chan view.View, 1)
go func() { received <- <-config.viewCh }()

fn := clearFilters(config)
assert.NoError(t, fn(nil, nil))

select {
case v := <-received:
	assert.Empty(t, v.Filters)
case <-time.After(time.Second):
	t.Fatal("handler did not send the cleared view on viewCh")
}
```
This keeps the existing assertions, drops the `close(config.viewCh)` (which only ever served to panic on a double send), and turns a 300 s package-wide hang into a 1 s named failure. If keeping the file's established `sync.WaitGroup` shape is preferred, at minimum add the `time.After` deadline around `wg.Wait()`.

findings.issue: Shared state between subcases. The task's acceptance criterion ('зависимость его кейсов от порядка выполнения либо устранена, либо явно задокументирована') is satisfied — the comment at lines 334-336 is accurate and load-bearing. But the anchor's preferred branch (remove the dependency) was not taken: the named `t.Run` subcases now LOOK independently addressable while they are not. Verified: `go test ./top/ -run 'Test_setFilter/clear-existing'` FAILS with `expected "Filters: regular expression cleared", actual "Filters: no filter on this column"`, because the `set` subcase that installs the filter is filtered out. Selecting a single subtest by name is a routine debugging action, so this will bite someone.
